subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust contract should OpenClaw support across memory-core, QMD, session memory, Active Memory, Memory Wiki, and public trust-policy config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but trust authority, schema shape, review/expiration semantics, plugin boundary, and public config policy are security/product decisions that should not be invented by an automated fix.

options.title: Design native trust contract first
options.body: Keep #7707 open and define framework-owned source authority, trust tiers, review/expiration gates, and retrieval weighting before implementation.

options.title: Fold under provenance foundation
options.body: Make #42647 and #48519 settle durable provenance first, then layer #7707 trust policy on top of that source model.

options.title: Leave scoring to plugins
options.body: Treat AKF/world-model-mcp as optional plugin paths and only add minimal OpenClaw hooks if maintainers do not want native trust policy.

recommendation.title: Design native trust contract first
recommendation.body: Keep #7707 open and define framework-owned source authority, trust tiers, review/expiration gates, and retrieval weighting before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current routing signal for the memory host SDK and memory-core contract boundary and has prior review context on this exact issue.
